questions.prompt: Water flows horizontally from speed \(2.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) to \(5.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find \(p_1-p_2\).
Water is accelerated from a very wide, nearly stationary region into a horizontal pipe by a pressure drop of \(18\,\mathrm{kPa}\). Find the pipe speed.
A small hole is \(0.80\,\mathrm{m}\) below the surface of a large open water tank. Estimate the exit speed.
questions.answer:
For a large open tank,
\[
v=\sqrt{2gh}
\]
\[
v=\sqrt{2(9.8)(0.80)}=4.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: A liquid flows steadily with the same speed at two points. Point 2 is \(3.0\,\mathrm{m}\) higher than point 1. For water, find \(p_1-p_2\).
questions.answer:
The speeds are equal, so the kinetic terms cancel:
\[
p_1+\rho gy_1=p_2+\rho gy_2
\]
\[
p_1-p_2=\rho g(y_2-y_1)=(1000)(9.8)(3.0)=2.94\times10^4\,\mathrm{Pa}
\]

questions.prompt: Water flows horizontally through a constriction where the area halves. If \(v_1=1.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), find \(v_2\) and \(p_1-p_2\).
Water flows from point 1 to point 2. The speed changes from \(2.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) to \(3.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), and point 2 is \(4.0\,\mathrm{m}\) higher. Find \(p_1-p_2\).
A Pitot-style measurement in air of density \(1.2\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}\) gives stagnation pressure \(540\,\mathrm{Pa}\) above static pressure. Find the air speed.
A hole in a large tank is \(1.25\,\mathrm{m}\) below the water surface and \(0.80\,\mathrm{m}\) above the floor. Estimate the horizontal range of the emerging water stream.
questions.answer:
The exit speed is
\[
v=\sqrt{2gh}=\sqrt{2(9.8)(1.25)}=4.95\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
The fall time from \(0.80\,\mathrm{m}\) is
\[
t=\sqrt{\frac{2(0.80)}{9.8}}=0.404\,\mathrm{s}
\]
The horizontal range is
\[
x=vt=(4.95)(0.404)=2.0\,\mathrm{m}
\]

questions.prompt: A horizontal Venturi tube carries water. The wide area is four times the narrow area, and the wide-section speed is \(1.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the pressure drop from wide to narrow section.
questions.answer:
Continuity gives \(v_2=4v_1=4.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). The pressure drop is
\[
p_1-p_2=\frac{1}{2}\rho(v_2^2-v_1^2)
\]
\[
p_1-p_2=\frac{1}{2}(1000)(16-1)=7.5\times10^3\,\mathrm{Pa}
\]

questions.prompt: A large open tank has a small outlet of area \(1.0\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{m^2}\), located \(2.0\,\mathrm{m}\) below the surface. Estimate the volume flow rate from the outlet.
questions.answer:
The exit speed is
\[
v=\sqrt{2gh}=\sqrt{2(9.8)(2.0)}=6.26\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
Therefore
\[
Q=av=(1.0\times10^{-4})(6.26)=6.3\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm{m^3\,s^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: Water flows horizontally. At section 1, \(p_1=2.20\times10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}\) and \(v_1=2.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). At section 2, \(v_2=7.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find \(p_2\).
A water jet exits vertically upward into the atmosphere from a nozzle fed by gauge pressure \(45\,\mathrm{kPa}\). Neglect losses and inlet speed. Estimate the maximum jet height.
Explain why a horizontal ideal-fluid streamline that speeds up must move toward lower pressure. Use Bernoulli's equation and also state the force interpretation.
questions.answer:
For horizontal ideal flow,
\[
p+\frac{1}{2}\rho v^2=\text{constant}
\]
If \(v\) increases, the kinetic term increases, so \(p\) must decrease. The force interpretation is the same: a fluid element speeds up only if there is a net force along the streamline, which requires higher pressure behind it than ahead of it.

questions.prompt: A horizontal pipe carries a liquid of unknown density. The speed increases from \(1.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) to \(4.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), and the pressure falls by \(6.0\,\mathrm{kPa}\). Find the density implied by Bernoulli's equation.

A siphon carries water from a large open reservoir to an outlet \(1.5\,\mathrm{m}\) below the reservoir surface. The siphon crest is \(0.80\,\mathrm{m}\) above the reservoir surface. Neglect losses and pipe-radius changes. Estimate the absolute pressure at the crest.
questions.answer:
The outlet is \(1.5\,\mathrm{m}\) below the reservoir surface, so
\[
\frac{v^2}{2g}=1.5\,\mathrm{m}
\]
At the crest, Bernoulli from the reservoir surface gives
\[
p_{\mathrm{atm}}=p_c+\frac{1}{2}\rho v^2+\rho g(0.80)
\]
Therefore
\[
p_c=p_{\mathrm{atm}}-\rho g(1.5+0.80)
\]
\[
p_c=1.01\times10^5-(1000)(9.8)(2.30)=7.8\times10^4\,\mathrm{Pa}
\]
This is absolute pressure, under the ideal no-loss model.

questions.prompt: A horizontal streamline has speed \(v(s)\) along distance coordinate \(s\). Starting from Bernoulli's equation, derive \(dp/ds\) in terms of \(v\) and \(dv/ds\). Interpret the sign when the flow accelerates.
questions.answer:
For horizontal flow,
\[
p+\frac{1}{2}\rho v^2=\text{constant}
\]
Differentiate with respect to \(s\):
\[
\frac{dp}{ds}+\rho v\frac{dv}{ds}=0
\]
so
\[
\frac{dp}{ds}=-\rho v\frac{dv}{ds}
\]
If the flow accelerates along \(s\), \(dv/ds>0\), so \(dp/ds<0\): pressure decreases downstream.

questions.prompt: For horizontal incompressible flow, section 1 has area \(A_1\), speed \(v_1\), and pressure \(p_1\). Section 2 has area \(A_2\). Derive \(p_1-p_2\) in terms of \(\rho\), \(v_1\), and \(k=A_1/A_2\).
questions.answer:
Continuity gives
\[
v_2=\frac{A_1}{A_2}v_1=kv_1
\]
Horizontal Bernoulli gives
\[
p_1-p_2=\frac{1}{2}\rho(v_2^2-v_1^2)
\]
Therefore
\[
p_1-p_2=\frac{1}{2}\rho v_1^2(k^2-1)
\]
For a constriction, \(k>1\), so the pressure drop is positive.

questions.prompt: A tank surface area \(A_T\) is not extremely large compared with a hole area \(a\). The water surface is height \(h\) above the hole, and both surface and hole are open to the atmosphere. Derive the hole speed using continuity and Bernoulli.
questions.answer:
Let the hole speed be \(v\). Continuity gives the downward surface speed
\[
v_T=\frac{a}{A_T}v
\]
Both points are open to the atmosphere, so pressures cancel:
\[
\frac{1}{2}\rho v_T^2+\rho gh=\frac{1}{2}\rho v^2
\]
Substitute \(v_T=(a/A_T)v\):
\[
v^2\left(1-\frac{a^2}{A_T^2}\right)=2gh
\]
\[
v=\sqrt{\frac{2gh}{1-(a/A_T)^2}}
\]
This reduces to \(\sqrt{2gh}\) when \(A_T\gg a\).

questions.prompt: A horizontal constriction has \(A_1/A_2=k>1\). Upstream pressure is \(p_1\), vapor pressure is \(p_v\), and density is \(\rho\). Derive the maximum upstream speed \(v_1\) that keeps the narrow-section pressure at or above \(p_v\).
questions.answer:
Continuity gives \(v_2=kv_1\). Bernoulli gives
\[
p_2=p_1+\frac{1}{2}\rho(v_1^2-v_2^2)
=p_1-\frac{1}{2}\rho v_1^2(k^2-1)
\]
Require \(p_2\ge p_v\):
\[
p_1-\frac{1}{2}\rho v_1^2(k^2-1)\ge p_v
\]
so
\[
v_1\le \sqrt{\frac{2(p_1-p_v)}{\rho(k^2-1)}}
\]

questions.prompt: A streamline connects points 1 and 2 in steady incompressible nonviscous flow. Derive a symbolic condition, using only \(p_1-p_2\), \(y_2-y_1\), and \(\rho\), for point 2 to have a larger speed than point 1. Interpret the condition physically.
questions.answer:
Bernoulli between the two points gives
\[
p_1-p_2=\frac{1}{2}\rho(v_2^2-v_1^2)+\rho g(y_2-y_1)
\]
Rearrange:
\[
v_2^2-v_1^2=\frac{2}{\rho}\left[p_1-p_2-\rho g(y_2-y_1)\right]
\]
Point 2 has the larger speed when
\[
p_1-p_2>\rho g(y_2-y_1)
\]
The pressure drop from 1 to 2 must exceed the pressure change needed merely to lift the fluid. Any remaining pressure drop appears as increased kinetic energy.
